rule: Haze index = 5th percentile of B02 (blue) top-of-atmosphere reflectance over the eligible pixels. If it is above 0.1403 (the maximum over all 203 training scenes, data/reports/haze_reference_training_v2.json), the scene is outside the training range: a model-positive pixel then counts as water only if its B11 (SWIR) reflectance is below 0.10, and the outcome is reported as inconclusive. Scenes within the training range are not changed.
history: 2026-10-28: an always-on B11 < 0.10 gate was chosen on validation (data/reports/swir_gate_validation_segmentation_v2.json; IoU 0.4555 vs 0.4565 ungated). On the held-out test split it lowered flood IoU from 0.157 to 0.081 (data/reports/evaluation_segmentation_v2_b11gate_test.json), so it is NOT applied to normal scenes. This decision used the test result and is disclosed in docs/milestone5_recovery_mission_report_2026-10-28.md.
The haze-conditional rule was added because a live image of Mumbai (18 Oct 2026) was hazier than any training image and the model marked dense urban blocks as water.
validation_status: The haze threshold comes from training data only. On the frozen splits it flags 3 of 24 validation scenes (EMSR265 Fontainebleau and Les Mureaux, haze index 0.175-0.211; pooled tiled flood IoU unchanged at 0.4565, three outcomes become inconclusive) and 0 of 22 test scenes (test metrics identical to the ungated model). It is a documented safety rule for out-of-range scenes, not a measured accuracy improvement.
